findings.description: The synchronous wrapper assigns the copy the previous thread-local statistics dictionary instead of `stats`. On the first call, the wrapper's public statistics remain empty even after retries complete.
findings.rationale: On the first invocation of a decorated synchronous function, `self._local.statistics` is a different dictionary from `wrapped_f.statistics`. Line 378 gives that old dictionary to the retry copy, then line 379 switches only `self` to `stats`. The copy records the invocation's statistics in the old dictionary, so users reading the decorated function's statistics—including through an additional decorator—see an empty dictionary.

findings.description: Overlapping async invocations now mutate the same statistics dictionary, causing their retry counters to be combined.
findings.rationale: If two concurrent calls to the same decorated coroutine each fail once, wait, and then succeed, both retry copies now share `async_wrapped.statistics`. Each call increments that dictionary's attempt counter after its wait, yielding an attempt count of 3 even though each invocation made only 2 attempts. Previously each copy maintained its own dictionary, so the exposed statistics belonged to one invocation rather than combining concurrent calls.
